Path: fleet decision — CI and merge-queue wall time set by the slowest required job | 缺项 | none

## Triage: first grade, `tooling` · `priority:p2` · `domain:devx` · `area:devpath` · `pm:blocked` behind #22014, as the body sequences it

Blocked-by: #22014

Triage seat (objectstack-wide, seat post #6015) · `session_01AavokzJ5DndAwitDXvKy4U` · 2026-10-07T13:12Z. ⛔ Not a claim, ⛔ not a dispatch.

Triage: lands in `scripts/partition-test-shards.mjs` (the derivation and `MAX_SHARD_OVER_MEAN = 1.3`, `:129`) and `scripts/test-shard-timings.json` ⇒ `domain:devx`; rationale: the lane of #16173, #16454, #16464 and #22014.

- **Why it enters, as a maintainer-directed `tooling` card:** the maintainer asked for these tasks (「CI 优化按照你的建议创建任务」, quoted in the body), and the first line names the guarded required contexts. So `triage-duties.md:34` is met. `:64` (close a p2/p3 `tooling` card while the lane queue holds an open P1, here #22080) does not apply to a maintainer-directed card, as on objectui#11762.
- **Why p2:** `Test Core (1/6)` sets CI and merge-queue wall time on every PR and every queue entry. It was measured at 34–36 minutes against 10–20 for the other shards.
- **Why blocked:** #22014 (dispatched) refreshes the shard-timings dataset this re-derivation reads. Claim after it lands, on the measured dataset.
- **Scope, as the body states it:** derive the balance on the runs that set the wall (the affected set on `pull_request` and `merge_group`), not only on full-run sums. The shard bound stays a ratio, and its pins are kept. The PR records the before-and-after wall on one PR run and one queue run.
